description: loop.sh never reads its own prior STATE.md before overwriting it -- unlike the reference model founder-loop.sh, which explicitly reads PREV_EARN from the existing STATE.md before acting (its INV-H1 invariant, founder-loop.sh:19-21) and persists prev_realised_earn_usdc for the next wake to compare against (founder-loop.sh:45-46). Combined with Capafy's revenue metric being only a 3-day trailing window (the field is literally named capafy_net_revenue_usd_3d, loop.sh:54) and no accumulation of history anywhere, the script cannot correctly evaluate its own stated GOAL line, which it writes verbatim every wake: 'LM Stripe revenue + Capafy subscription revenue > Dais monthly spend (~$200)' (loop.sh:50). A wake cadence gap greater than 3 days permanently loses visibility into that gap's Capafy revenue (it is never re-summed or carried forward), and there is no mechanism analogous to founder-loop's ledger-summed cumulative TOTAL to reconcile a rolling 3-day snapshot against a MONTHLY spend comparison.

evidence.snippet:
DIR="${LMCAP_DIR:-$HERE}"; STATE_MD="$DIR/state/STATE.md"; mkdir -p "$DIR/state"
... (no read of $STATE_MD anywhere before it is overwritten at line 57) ...
echo "capafy_net_revenue_usd_3d: $CAP_REV"

fix: Either read+carry-forward a running monthly total in STATE.md (mirroring founder-loop's PREV_EARN pattern), or call a Capafy endpoint that returns actual monthly/cumulative revenue instead of a 3-day trend, and document how the number is reconciled against the ~$200/month goal.
